tagline: West from Troy on a mail route that lasted eighteen months.
intro: The byway starts on US 36 east of Troy and wanders south on K-7 and K-20 through Bendena, Denton and Everest, west on US 73 to Horton and north on US 75 to Fairview. From there it is about 50 miles west on US 36 to Marysville, then a last turn north on K-148 to the Hollenberg station near Hanover.

The riders ran for only 18 months, until October 1861. Richard Francis Burton, passing through in 1860, was not taken with the towns. He called Troy "a few wretched shanties" and Seneca "a city consisting of a few shanties", and said Marysville thrived "by selling whiskey to ruffians of all descriptions."

moments.title: Seneca
moments.text: The Smith Hotel at Fourth and Main was the first Pony Express home station west of St. Joseph, and the town museum now stands across from where it was.

moments.title: Marysville
moments.text: The 1859 limestone barn downtown is the only Pony Express home station still on its original site, in a town that also keeps a colony of all-black squirrels.

moments.title: Hollenberg Pony Express Station
moments.text: Riders slept in the loft of this cottonwood-frame ranch house, where the Hollenbergs kept a shop and a tavern, and it is the most intact Pony Express station left in the country.
